claims.text: Introducing ordered oxygen complexes will reduce post-exposure toughness degradation in a high-entropy alloy.
Ordered oxygen complexes can be introduced by adjusting niobium and oxygen contents.
The proposed intervention applies to an as-designed, high-performance multicomponent high-entropy alloy.
Ordered oxygen complexes enhance alloy strength.
Ordered oxygen complexes enhance alloy ductility.
The simultaneous enhancement of strength and ductility by ordered oxygen complexes reduces toughness degradation after prolonged heating.
The treated alloy will retain toughness better after heating than an untreated high-entropy-alloy baseline.
The relevant exposure-temperature boundary is 800–1200 degrees Celsius.
The relevant exposure duration is 1000 hours.
The hypothesis is intended to apply under both quasi-static and high-strain-rate loading.
Tensile yield strength, ductility, and toughness should be measured after the defined exposure.
A lack of statistically significant improvement in toughness retention relative to the untreated alloy would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention changes Nb and oxygen contents, so the treated and untreated materials cannot be otherwise identical in composition. This also creates a confound between OOC formation and direct compositional effects unless composition-matched controls are included.
